keyVerseText: And in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, which is the eighth month, was the house finished throughout all the parts thereof, and according to all the fashion of it. So was he seven years in building it. through out: or, with all the parts thereof, and with all the ordinances thereof
rootMeaning: The root of בּוּל (Bûwl) connects to the concept of growth and produce, specifically relating to food or stock derived from the earth. This etymology emphasizes an agricultural sense of increase or outgrowth, which enriches the understanding of the word beyond its common English gloss as simply a month name. It suggests a period associated with natural productivity and provision.
usageInScripture: This word appears only once in Scripture, where it is used as the name of the eighth Hebrew month, Bul. The consistent translation as 'Bul' across its sole occurrence highlights its function primarily as a temporal marker rather than a thematic or conceptual term. This limited usage underscores its role in marking sacred or historical time within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Theological reflection on בּוּל reveals the significance of God’s provision and timing in the unfolding of redemptive history. As the eighth month, Bul situates events within God’s ordained calendar, reminding believers of divine sovereignty over seasons and the rhythm of life. The root meaning tied to increase and produce points to God as the ultimate source of growth and sustenance, both physically and spiritually. Recognizing this deepens faith in God's faithful provision and perfect timing in the fulfillment of His promises.
keyVerseReflection: 1 Kings 6:38 states, 'And in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, which is the eighth month, was the house finished throughout all the parts thereof.' The use of Bul here precisely dates the completion of Solomon’s temple, highlighting God’s providential timing. The name Bul, with its root meaning connected to increase and produce, subtly underscores the fruitful outcome of faithful labor and divine blessing in the building of the temple, a central place for worship and encounter with God.
